title: My Androgynous Boyfriend
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Wako, a hardworking manga editor who pays little attention to her looks, lives with her boyfriend Meguru, a model and clothing clerk in the genderless fashion scene with a large social-media following. People around them often misread Meguru's gender and the nature of their relationship, while friends like Sasame, an androgynous idol who wants to be seen as manly, explore their own self-images.
life_message: Love means supporting each other as you are, whatever others expect a man or woman to look like.

content.note: Adult couple living together (MangaUpdates Live-in Lover); ANN calls it a sweet romance; MangaDex rates it safe.
Fashion, makeup and social-media influence are central (AniList Fashion, Makeup).

dominant: Expressive individualism; questioning gender norms; supportive partnership

frames.aligns: Meguru's faithful devotion and mutual care between partners.
frames.concerns: Unmarried cohabitation and a message questioning sex-based roles.
Cohabitation; emphasis on appearance and vanity.
Holiness and modesty in appearance; cohabitation.

frames.aligns: Love serving the neighbor at home.

frames.concerns: Focus on fashion and adornment conflicts with plainness.
ANN says it does not go far with gender issues.
Men imitating women's dress is discouraged in hadith; cohabitation.

frames.aligns: Gender-nonconforming man in a loving relationship; AniList lists bisexual and asexual characters.
frames.concerns: ANN notes it raises gender issues without doing enough with them.

frames.aligns: Freedom of self-presentation and equal partnership.
Balance of masculine and feminine in one person.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Misunderstandings met with patience rather than retaliation (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Couple and workplace friends at center.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Egalitarian partnership; older woman, younger man (MangaUpdates).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Publisher blurb frames it as breaking with tradition.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Fashion, makeup and self-presentation are the core.

folkways.japan: Reflects Japan's genderless-danshi fashion subculture and long workdays in the publishing industry.

delivery.evidence: ANN's Silverman says it raises gender issues but does not do enough with them, suggesting a light touch.

personified.ideology: Wanting to be seen as conventionally manly

delivery.note: Conventional gender expectations appear mostly through misunderstandings by bystanders, while Sasame's wish for manliness is treated with sympathy.

winners_losers: Wako and Meguru's relationship thrives; outside assumptions are gently shown as mistaken; self-expression gets the sympathy.
